transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up when I really should be staying put. Like during sprint planning at work, or even mortgage calls, I’ll suddenly feel like I need water or I should check something in the other room. I know it’s not the right time, but I still end up doing it.
Do you often feel restless or find it hard to stay seated even when you know you should?

Yes. Even if I’m sitting still and I look calm, inside I feel kind of wound up, like there’s this pressure to move or switch to something else. Sometimes I need to do something with my hands, or I start feeling like I’m going to crawl out of my skin if I just stay there.
Do you often feel worried or anxious about things, even when there’s no clear reason for concern?
Not really, no. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious for no reason or that worry is the main issue.
Do you often have trouble waiting your turn, like in lines or during conversations, and feel the urge to jump in or do something else instead of waiting?

Yes, that happens. Like in stand-up meetings, waiting for my turn to talk can make me weirdly irritated, and I’ll catch myself checking the time or wanting to cut in. Same thing if I’m on hold with the bank — I know I should just wait, but I get impatient and feel like I need to do something else.
Do you often start tasks or projects without finishing them, like moving on to something new before completing what you started?

Yes, that happens. A common example is if my husband asks me to call the insurance company, upload a form, and then email the confirmation. I’ll usually do the first part, maybe even most of it, but then the last step somehow just sits there unfinished until he reminds me.

Do these feelings of restlessness, impulsivity, or difficulty finishing tasks happen in different parts of your life, like at home, at work, or in social situations, or are they mostly limited to one area?

It’s not just one area, no. I notice it at work and at home mostly. At work, people have to follow up with me more than they used to, and at home my husband ends up reminding me about things I said I’d handle. It’s not severe, but it’s starting to create some friction, and I worry I’m becoming the unreliable one with planning or finishing tasks even though I’m really trying.
